source.creator: Walt Disney / Ub Iwerks
source.basis: Full-figure side profile at a spoked ship's wheel, whistling and tapping his foot as in the 1928 opening scene: round offset ears, white face mask with tall black eye and long snout ending in a black nose, no gloves, rubber-hose limbs, shorts with two white buttons, big oval shoes, long thin tail; black, white and grey only.
source.notice: Based on the 1928 short Steamboat Willie (public domain in the US). Not affiliated with or endorsed by Disney.

source.creator: Walt Disney / Ub Iwerks
source.basis: A jaunty rubber-hose walk on the deck with arms and tail swinging, keeping the 1928 black-and-white design (no gloves, two-button shorts, big shoes).
source.notice: Based on the 1928 short Steamboat Willie (public domain in the US). Not affiliated with or endorsed by Disney.

source.creator: Walt Disney / Ub Iwerks
source.basis: A little jig with crouch, hop, kicks and toe taps, turning to face the other way, in the spirit of the 1928 short's musical antics; black, white and grey only.
source.notice: Based on the 1928 short Steamboat Willie (public domain in the US). Not affiliated with or endorsed by Disney.

source.creator: Walt Disney / Ub Iwerks
source.basis: The 1928 girl mouse in side profile with her small hat perched between the ears and a bobbing flower, eyelash, dark skirt with white petticoat frill and big oval shoes, waving with a little hop; black, white and grey only, no later bow design.
source.notice: Based on the girl mouse as she appears in the 1928 shorts Steamboat Willie and Plane Crazy (public domain in the US). Not affiliated with or endorsed by Disney.

source.creator: Walt Disney / Ub Iwerks
source.basis: The 1928 girl mouse crouches, springs, flares her skirt and lands facing the other way; same 1928 hat-and-flower design in black, white and grey.
source.notice: Based on the girl mouse as she appears in the 1928 shorts Steamboat Willie and Plane Crazy (public domain in the US). Not affiliated with or endorsed by Disney.

source.creator: E. C. Segar
source.basis: Newspaper-ink look: white sailor cap, squinting eye, jutting chin, black shirt with sailor collar and corncob pipe, puffing smoke rings on a newsprint background. No spinach (introduced later).
source.notice: Based on the sailor's 1929 debut in E. C. Segar's Thimble Theatre newspaper strip (public domain in the US and most countries). Character names and marks belong to their owners; not affiliated with or endorsed by King Features.

source.creator: E. C. Segar
source.basis: Wind-up, a straight punch with modest (not exaggerated) forearms and a starburst impact, then a satisfied puff of the pipe; 1929 strip design, no spinach.
source.notice: Based on the sailor's 1929 debut in E. C. Segar's Thimble Theatre newspaper strip (public domain in the US and most countries). Character names and marks belong to their owners; not affiliated with or endorsed by King Features.

source.creator: E. C. Segar
source.basis: A shaking, open-mouthed chuckle with the pipe bobbing and little smoke puffs popping out with each laugh, after the 1929 strip design.
source.notice: Based on the sailor's 1929 debut in E. C. Segar's Thimble Theatre newspaper strip (public domain in the US and most countries). Character names and marks belong to their owners; not affiliated with or endorsed by King Features.

source.creator: Walt Disney Productions
source.basis: A lanky white pup with a long snout, black floppy ear, black nose and thin black tail, nose to the ground following a trail of paw prints, as the bloodhounds track the escaped convict in The Chain Gang; black, white and grey only.
source.notice: Based on the unnamed bloodhound pups in the 1930 shorts The Chain Gang and The Picnic (public domain in the US); a forerunner of the dog later named Pluto. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Disney.

source.creator: Walt Disney Productions
source.basis: The same 1930 bloodhound pup standing alert, panting with tongue out, floppy ear bouncing and tail wagging; black, white and grey only.
source.notice: Based on the unnamed bloodhound pups in the 1930 shorts The Chain Gang and The Picnic (public domain in the US); a forerunner of the dog later named Pluto. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Disney.

source.creator: Winsor McCay
source.basis: The friendly sauropod bows her head to the ground for the audience, then rises and dances from foot to foot, as in McCay's 1914 vaudeville film.
source.notice: Based on Winsor McCay's 1914 animated film Gertie the Dinosaur (public domain in the US and most countries). Not affiliated with any rights holder.

source.creator: Winsor McCay
source.basis: Bite by bite she eats a tree, each mouthful sliding down her long neck, until a new sapling sprouts; a nod to the tree-eating gag in the 1914 film.
source.notice: Based on Winsor McCay's 1914 animated film Gertie the Dinosaur (public domain in the US and most countries). Not affiliated with any rights holder.

source.creator: Winsor McCay
source.basis: She dips her head and gulps the lake dry, gulps travelling up her neck and her belly swelling, then rain refills it; after the famous drinking scene in the 1914 film.
source.notice: Based on Winsor McCay's 1914 animated film Gertie the Dinosaur (public domain in the US and most countries). Not affiliated with any rights holder.

source.creator: George Herriman
source.basis: Ignatz lobs a brick at Krazy, who takes it as a token of love, as in Herriman's early daily strips; desert mesa nods to Coconino County.
source.notice: Based on George Herriman's early Krazy Kat newspaper strips (1913 onward; public domain in the US and most countries). Character names and marks belong to their owners; not affiliated with or endorsed by King Features.

source.creator: Winsor McCay
source.basis: Nemo in his nightgown riding the long-legged walking bed over the rooftops, after McCay's July 1908 New York Herald Sunday page.
source.notice: Based on Winsor McCay's Little Nemo in Slumberland (New York Herald, 1905-1911; public domain in the US and most countries). Not affiliated with any rights holder.
